name: Cleveland-class light cruiser
blurb: A light cruiser, planned as a friendly escort.
history:
The Cleveland class was a group of light cruisers built for the U.S. Navy during World War II, armed with 6-inch guns, which the Navy favored for their rate of fire over the slower 8-inch. Fifty-two were ordered and 36 completed: 27 as cruisers and nine as Independence-class light aircraft carriers.

Late in the war the added light anti-aircraft guns made the ships top-heavy. Most were deactivated within a few years of the war's end, though six became missile ships, and USS Little Rock survives as a museum ship.
